concerns.artifact: the guard activation command published to the owner

finding: The package hash published as the --expect-hash value for the guard activation did not belong to the commit it was published for. The owner's dry run refused it and installed nothing, which is exactly what --expect-hash is for.

question_1_provenance.belongs_to: an uncommitted worktree state: the HEAD tree with the superseded longest-prefix version of _root_prefix in tools/guard/fixture.py, which existed for a few minutes before the symlink defect in it was fixed and was never committed.
question_1_provenance.proof: Replacing that one function in the committed HEAD tree and rebuilding reproduces the published value exactly.
question_1_provenance.installer_value_belongs_to: every commit of the B0c range: tools/guard changed only in the first of them and not afterwards, so the package digest is identical for 6feb7ce through a4a6e7f.
question_1_provenance.carried_forward_detail: The same value was published for 87ca814 and again for a4a6e7f. It was derived once, before either commit existed, and never re-derived from either. That is the defect: not a wrong calculation, but a value that was repeated instead of derived.

question_2_artifacts.method: Search for the value across the tracked tree at HEAD and across the whole worktree including untracked files.
question_2_artifacts.that_value_is: the package of the guard installation that is actually active (1.1.0), read from active.json. It is correct and unrelated to the published candidate value; the acceptance record carries no candidate hash field at all.

mechanical_evidence: No block manifest passes --expect-hash or --expect-version; the search over config/gates/blocks returns nothing.

The guard-activation gate mode builds the candidate package itself at run time and compares it against active.json. It accepts no declared expectation value, so no gate could consume the published one.
The committed B0c evidence contains no package hash at all; the only digests in it are raw log digests.
The published value occurs in no artifact of the block.
question_3_did_it_carry_a_statement.where_it_did_appear: Only in the message to the owner. It was an instruction, not an artifact, and no gate result or acceptance statement rests on it.
question_3_did_it_carry_a_statement.why_this_is_not_an_excuse: The instruction is still an output of the block, and it was wrong. What the evidence establishes is narrower and is stated narrowly: the machine status is not affected. The defect in the published instruction is real and is the reason for rule R6.

question_4_why_no_check_caught_it.what_it_does: It builds the package twice from the same source and compares the two digests to each other. That establishes reproducibility of one source state.
question_4_why_no_check_caught_it.what_it_never_did: It never relates a digest to a commit. A value derived from any source is reproducible in that sense, including one derived from an uncommitted worktree.
question_4_why_no_check_caught_it.missing_check: There was no check that a published expectation value belongs to the commit it is claimed for. That check did not exist and now does.

rule.statement: Every expectation value of an owner action must be reproducibly derivable from exactly the commit and the artifact the action refers to, and that derivation belongs to the acceptance evidence.

corrected_expectation.derivation: git archive <commit> unpacked into a scratch tree; tools/guardpkg/build.py --source <tree>; the reported package_sha256 is the value. Built from the commit object, never from a worktree.

historical_evidence.statement: The committed B0c evidence and the B0c acceptance record are not edited. Their bytes and their digests stay exactly as they are. This is a note beside them, the same procedure as the erratum to the frozen baseline.

verification_after_the_rule.note: A fresh run against the amended state. It does not replace the committed acceptance evidence of B0c, which stays bound to the acceptance commit.
